item.title: USDA invests $65 million in farm conservation innovation grants
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture announced Wednesday it is awarding $65 million across 34 Conservation Innovation Grants to help farmers and ranchers develop and test new tools, technologies, and practices that conserve natural resources while improving farm operations. The Natural Resources Conservation Service is splitting the awards between…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture announced Wednesday it is awarding $65 million across 34 Conservation Innovation Grants to help farmers and ranchers develop and test new tools, technologies, and practices that conserve natural resources while improving farm operations.

The Natural Resources Conservation Service is splitting the awards between two programs: $50 million for 16 On-Farm Trials projects that focus on widespread adoption and evaluation of innovative conservation approaches in partnership with agricultural producers, and $15 million for 18 Classic projects that develop new tools, technologies, and strategies to support next-generation conservation efforts on working lands.

According to NRCS Chief Colton L. Buckley, the grants represent an effort to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions that keep working lands productive for future generations. "These grants will lay the foundation to help producers improve their operations, conserve natural resources, and strengthen the future of American agriculture," Buckley said in a statement.

Among the awarded projects are an Idaho virtual fencing system designed for small and mid-sized livestock operations and an Illinois project developing a decision tool to help farmers optimize nitrogen application for increased profitability and soil health. Since 2004, NRCS has invested $594 million to fund 957 innovative projects through the Conservation Innovation Grants program.

item.title: Santa Rosa Extension offers cottage foods business class Nov. 5
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The UF/IFAS Santa Rosa County Extension Service is hosting an Introduction to Cottage Foods class Thursday, November 5, from 6 to 7:30 p.m. at their offices in Milton. The workshop covers Florida cottage food law, what qualifies as a cottage food product, food safety basics for home-based production, labeling requirements, and where cottage food…
item.content:encoded:
The UF/IFAS Santa Rosa County Extension Service is hosting an Introduction to Cottage Foods class Thursday, November 5, from 6 to 7:30 p.m. at their offices in Milton.

The workshop covers Florida cottage food law, what qualifies as a cottage food product, food safety basics for home-based production, labeling requirements, and where cottage food operators can legally sell their goods. The class costs $10 and is designed for people interested in starting a small food business from home.

Pre-registration is required by Tuesday, November 3, through Eventbrite. Space is limited and walk-ins won't be accepted. To sign up, visit https://www.eventbrite.com/e/introduction-to-cottage-foods-milton-fl-tickets-1999122417967. For questions, call the extension office at 850-623-3868. Anyone needing accessibility accommodations should contact jbreslawski@ufl.edu at least two weeks in advance.

item.title: DeSantis Awards $100M for Florida Springs, Water Supply Projects
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced $100 million in funding for 45 water protection projects across Florida on Wednesday, with awards split between springs restoration and alternative water supply initiatives. The Springs Restoration Grant Program is directing $50 million to 23 projects aimed at improving water quality and spring flow, with a focus on…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced $100 million in funding for 45 water protection projects across Florida on Wednesday, with awards split between springs restoration and alternative water supply initiatives.

The Springs Restoration Grant Program is directing $50 million to 23 projects aimed at improving water quality and spring flow, with a focus on reducing nitrogen pollution. According to the Governor's Press Office, the funded projects are expected to collectively cut Total Nitrogen by more than 55,000 pounds annually. Major recipients include Citrus County, which received $3 million for septic-to-sewer conversion work that will benefit Crystal River Springs and other local water bodies, and Volusia County, which got $3 million for a septic upgrade incentive program to benefit DeLeon Spring.

The remaining $50 million supports 22 alternative water supply projects designed to reduce reliance on traditional freshwater sources and produce over 60 million gallons of water per day. Projects focus on expanding reclaimed water use, aquifer recharge, and conservation. Tampa Bay Water received $10 million to expand surface water treatment capacity, while seven Polk County communities will share $12.6 million for brackish water diversification projects.

Since 2019, Florida has invested $480 million in springs restoration efforts, resulting in an estimated annual nitrogen reduction of approximately 900,000 pounds per year, according to the Governor's office.

item.title: Senator Moody Honors Seven Florida Officers for Life-Saving Heroism
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody recognized seven law enforcement officers from South Florida on National First Responders Day today for extraordinary acts of bravery and lifesaving service. The honorees—drawn from Miami-Dade County, Homestead, Miami, and Bay Harbor Islands—each received a Florida's Finest Award from the senator in recognition of going above…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody recognized seven law enforcement officers from South Florida on National First Responders Day today for extraordinary acts of bravery and lifesaving service. The honorees—drawn from Miami-Dade County, Homestead, Miami, and Bay Harbor Islands—each received a Florida's Finest Award from the senator in recognition of going above and beyond the call of duty.

Among those recognized was Miami-Dade County Sheriff's Deputy Leonard Cantave, who suffered life-threatening injuries in December 2025 when he pushed a fellow officer out of the path of an oncoming vehicle on Florida's Turnpike, taking the impact himself. Also honored was Homestead Police Officer Carston Addison, who rescued a child from a retention pond and later prevented the juvenile from self-harm during the same incident. Miami Police Officers David Alvarez-Daza and James Fraser were recognized for their quick thinking in resuscitating a seven-day-old infant who was unresponsive and unable to breathe during an emergency call on August 20.

"Florida's law enforcement officers work so hard to keep us safe, and it is always a privilege to thank them personally for all they do for Floridians," Moody said. The full group of honorees also included Miami Police Officers Sonia Augustin and Napoleon Workmond, and Town of Bay Harbor Islands Commander Tomas Rego.

item.title: Florida AG Uthmeier Pursues Fetal Personhood Legal Strategy, Dems Warn of Abortion Ban Risk
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is advancing a legal strategy centered on establishing fetal personhood, according to recent reporting by CBS News Miami. During an appearance on an anti-abortion podcast earlier this month, Uthmeier said he views a Broward County surrogacy case as an opportunity to "bring the conversation of fetal…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is advancing a legal strategy centered on establishing fetal personhood, according to recent reporting by CBS News Miami. During an appearance on an anti-abortion podcast earlier this month, Uthmeier said he views a Broward County surrogacy case as an opportunity to "bring the conversation of fetal personhood and life front and center," and expressed that he's "excited" to "fight for life" using "any tool we have above and beyond" Florida's current six-week abortion ban.

Uthmeier is leveraging the surrogacy dispute to challenge Florida law by arguing that surrogacy agreements violate the 13th Amendment—the constitutional provision that abolished slavery. Legal experts warn that if his approach succeeds, it could eliminate all abortion access in Florida, including exceptions for rape and incest, and severely restrict IVF and surrogacy options for families seeking assisted reproduction. The infant at the center of the case has already returned to France with its parents, but Uthmeier is continuing the legal fight, with an appeals hearing scheduled for January.

Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried criticized Uthmeier's strategy, noting that nearly 60 percent of Florida voters supported a 2024 constitutional amendment protecting abortion access—though it fell short of the 60 percent threshold required for passage. "He's acting like that vote never happened," Fried said. Uthmeier, an unelected attorney general and former chief of staff to Governor Ron DeSantis, has previously intervened in abortion cases, including blocking a 17-year-old's access to judicial waiver approval and convincing an appeals court to strike down Florida's judicial bypass law.

The 2026 edition, titled "Rock the Runway: Living Art," will feature performances spanning everything from Mozart to Missy Elliott, according to…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Opera is bringing back its annual Foo Foo Fest for its fourth year, this time with an expanded lineup that promises to blend classical and contemporary music with visual art and runway fashion.

The 2026 edition, titled "Rock the Runway: Living Art," will feature performances spanning everything from Mozart to Missy Elliott, according to reporting in InWeekly. The event marks a new collaboration with Ballet Pensacola, bringing dance into the mix alongside opera, pop, and rock performances.

The festival aims to introduce new audiences to opera while entertaining longtime fans through an unconventional theatrical experience that treats the stage as a canvas for multiple art forms. Foo Foo Fest has become one of Pensacola's signature cultural events, drawing crowds who appreciate the genre-blending approach to live performance.

item.title: Shumaker Advisors launches roundtable series with Amendment 3 discussion
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Shumaker Advisors is launching The Connection Point, a new roundtable series aimed at bringing together business, civic, and government leaders across Northwest Florida for discussions on regional opportunities and challenges. The inaugural event, held in partnership with the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce, will focus on Amendment 3. The…
item.content:encoded:
Shumaker Advisors is launching The Connection Point, a new roundtable series aimed at bringing together business, civic, and government leaders across Northwest Florida for discussions on regional opportunities and challenges.

The inaugural event, held in partnership with the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce, will focus on Amendment 3. The roundtable is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 1 p.m., and will be led by Escambia County Commissioner Mike Kohler and Walter Pierce. According to a press release, the discussion will examine the amendment from multiple perspectives to help attendees understand the issue and its potential implications.

Sara Lefevers, Vice President at Shumaker Advisors, said the series is designed to create "a trusted space" for regional leaders to exchange ideas on complex issues and identify collaboration opportunities. "Northwest Florida's continued success depends on leaders from across the region having a trusted space to exchange ideas, better understand complex issues, and identify opportunities to work together," Lefevers said in the release.

The firm plans to announce additional roundtables and topics as the series continues. Those interested can register for the inaugural event through Shumaker Advisors.

Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia Children's Trust has distributed $3,639,575 in Bright Beginnings grants to support early childhood development and family services across the county.

Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with developmental concerns, and expanded services reaching into the Century and North Escambia County areas that have historically had fewer resources.

In total, 11 different projects were selected to receive funding through the competitive grant process. The awards reflect the trust's focus on giving young children in Escambia County a strong start through evidence-based programs and increased access to specialized care.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola and North Escambia are in for a stretch of pleasant fall weather over the next few days, with mostly sunny skies and warm afternoons expected through Friday. Highs should reach the upper 70s to low 80s, making it ideal weather for outdoor activities, while nights cool to the mid-50s to lower 60s. The pattern breaks down heading into the weekend, according to local forecasts, when rain chances increase. Residents should enjoy the dry weather window while it lasts and keep an eye on weekend forecasts for timing and intensity of potential precipitation.

item.content:encoded:
Two adults lost their home early Tuesday morning when a fire broke out in a two-story residence in Cantonment. Escambia County Fire Rescue responded around 4:53 a.m. to a house in the 2200 block of Riddle Road, off East Kingsfield Road, according to North Escambia. Firefighters found the blaze concentrated on the upper level of the home.

The displaced residents have been accounted for. No additional details on injuries, the fire's cause, or damage estimates were immediately available. The county fire department has not yet released further information about the incident.
